description: Run ONE read-only SQL statement against a registered foreign Postgres connection (by connection_name). Read leaders only (SELECT/WITH/EXPLAIN/SHOW/VALUES/TABLE) — the connection is read-only at the server, so any write or DDL is refused. The result is ALWAYS written to the caller-supplied output_tsv_path, never returned inline, at any size. This connection targets an arbitrary customer database, so there is no vendor-imposed row ceiling to defer to; the limit below is entirely our own policy. Defaults to 500 rows to avoid exhausting the target database and disk, and to discourage pulling all rows for client-side filtering that a WHERE clause should do instead. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 1000) — both are required together, and a row_limit above 1000 is refused rather than silently clamped. For pulls beyond 1000 rows, use export_query instead (same override mechanism, hard cap 50000). Use list_connections to discover registered names. When the goal is validating that records exist or picking one to act on next, prefer selecting stable ID columns over email addresses or other PII-bearing fields — the query decides what columns come back, so a narrower SELECT is both cheaper and lower-exposure.
embedding_description: Run an ad-hoc read-only SELECT against a registered external Postgres database and land the columns and rows in a workspace TSV file -- never inline, at any size. Defaults to 500 rows unless acknowledged otherwise. Prefer selecting stable ID columns over PII-bearing fields for a validation read. The everyday query surface over foreign business databases.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Foreign Postgres query written to a workspace TSV
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with path (the written .tsv file in the operator's workspace), columns (ordered names), row_count, and truncated (true when row_count hit the effective limit -- more rows may exist).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the write: the path, the row_count, and the column list. The file may contain potentially sensitive corporate database content (data_sensitivity 0.5) -- name the path for downstream use (open it, feed it to create_spreadsheet_from_files, join it with other exports) but never inline its contents into context. If truncated is true, say so and point to export_query or an acknowledged row_limit override for the rest.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run a read-only SQL query against a registered foreign Postgres connection and write the result to a workspace TSV file.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: external_pg.invalid_params: missing connection_name/sql/output_tsv_path, the path's parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, or row_limit exceeded the 1000 hard cap. external_pg.export_path_refused: output_tsv_path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry (an empty export_allowed_roots refuses every write by default). external_pg.connection_unknown: no connection registered under that name. external_pg.read_only_violation: the statement is a write/DDL or is not a permitted read leader. external_pg.query_failed: a SQL syntax or missing-object error in your query. external_pg.auth_failed / external_pg.permission_denied: the registered credential was rejected. external_pg.timeout: the query exceeded the statement timeout. external_pg.platform_db_refused: the connection targets the platform's own database (refused).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: external_pg.invalid_params naming the override pair: pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-row default); a row_limit above 1000 must go through export_query instead. external_pg.invalid_params with a missing-parent message: create the parent directory first. external_pg.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root; if export_allowed_roots is empty, add the operator's export directory to the external_postgres_plugin config (profile/config/plugins/external_postgres_plugin.json). external_pg.connection_unknown: run list_connections to see registered names. external_pg.read_only_violation: submit a single SELECT/WITH/EXPLAIN/SHOW/VALUES/TABLE statement. external_pg.query_failed: fix the SQL. external_pg.timeout: narrow the query or add a LIMIT. external_pg.auth_failed/permission_denied: ask the operator to re-check the registered connection.
